Plugin update dialogs can display the corresponding plugin release history in the app

`auto.registerEvent(name, listener, options?)` gains optional de-duplication and debouncing: `{ distinct: 'window' | 'source' | true | (event) => key, within?: 500 }` drops repeated events with the same key within the window (such as the several `WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED` events of one window transition), `{ debounce: ms }` delivers only the last event of a burst once it has been quiet for that long; both off by default

Shizuku joins root and the secure settings permission as an unattended way of enabling the accessibility service (used when neither of the other two is available, writing the system setting through the Shizuku user service): a new "Enable accessibility service with Shizuku automatically" switch (on by default) in the settings page and in the settings section of the accessibility service manager, plus a "Shizuku access" row in the manager's status section

New `auto.setFlags()` flag `appWindowsFallback`: while the system does not provide the active window root yet (right after the accessibility service has been bound; on Android 8.0 possibly until the next window change), selectors and `auto.root` / `auto.rootInActiveWindow` / `auto.windowRoots` fall back to the roots of the application windows of the window list (focused window first); off by default

New `UiObject` methods `contentInvalid()` / `contextClickable()` / `multiLine()` / `dismissable()` (in the style of `clickable()` and the other boolean property methods, mirroring the existing compat accessors `isContentInvalid` etc.)

New methods on widget collections (the arrays returned by `find()` / `untilFind()` / `children()` / `siblings()` and the like): `at(i)` (negative counts from the end, null out of range), `first()` / `last()` (null when empty), `nonNull()` (drops the null entries), `slice(start?, end?)` (index rules of `Array.prototype.slice`, the result still carries the collection methods), and the per-node variants `performActionEach(action, ...args)` / `clickEach()` / `longClickEach()` / `scrollForwardEach()` / `scrollBackwardEach()` / `setTextEach(text)` (a boolean array, every node attempted; the boolean AND semantics of the existing `performAction` / `click()` etc. are unchanged); `filter` / `map` / `forEach` / `some` / `every` / `indexOf` / `for...of` are the array's own operations and keep working as before
Accessibility coordinate-click helpers: smartClickBounds, clickBoundsIfExists, clickBoundsAny, Flow wait and delayed clickBounds steps, and their aliases
Flow instance steps clickIfExists / clickAny / findAny, optional whenPresent branches and bounded asynchronous repeatUntil loops

New asynchronous, chainable wait API: `waitAsync(cond, timeout?, interval?)` (aliases `wait.async` / `auto.wait` / `flow.wait`) returns a `Flow` object instead of blocking the script; the condition may be a selector (string / regex / `UiSelector` / object / array), a function, a `UiObject`, a `Flow` or a `Promise`; a chain may continue with node actions (`click` / `longClick` / `setText` / `scrollForward` etc.), global actions (`back` / `home` / `swipe` etc.), `sleep` / `timeout` / `retry` / `scope` and the callbacks `then` / `catch` (`else`) / `finally` / `map` / `filter` / `peek` / `run`, yields its result through `sync()` / `await()` / `toPromise()` and is cancelled with `cancel()`; global entry points `waitThenClick` (`clickWait`), `waitForStable`, `waitForStableThenClick` (`clickWhenStable`), `clickWhenStableAfter`, `waitForVisible`, `waitForHidden` (`waitForGone`), plus in the `flow` (`$flow`) namespace `waitUntil` / `waitWhile` / `waitForActivity` / `waitForPackage` / `waitThenLongClick` / `sleep` (`delay`) / `run` / `of` / `all` / `race` / `any` / `cancelAll` / `Flow` / `pending`; blocking steps run on a per-script worker pool (`flow-<id>-<n>` threads, one serial lane per chain, so independent chains run concurrently) and callbacks are posted back to the script thread that created the chain (usable in UI mode, though `sync()` is forbidden on the UI thread), and every pending chain is cancelled and the pool stopped when the script exits; failures reject with a `FlowError` (an `Error` carrying `code` / `step` / `selector` / `elapsed` / `attempts` / `reason`) whose code is `TIMEOUT` / `ACTION_FAILED` / `CANCELLED` / `A11Y_UNAVAILABLE` / `INVALID_TARGET`; `flow.defaults({ timeout, interval, stableFor, strictActions, trace })` sets the per-script defaults (a read without arguments) and `flow.trace(true)` logs every step's start / end / elapsed time / outcome to the console; the convenience steps `clickAfter(min, max?)` / `longClickAfter` / `clickWhenStableAfter` and `sleep(min, max?)` accept a `"±delta"` string like the global `sleep`; the synchronous `wait()` is unchanged

High-level automation tools on both the `automator` module and the global scope: `smartClick(target, options?)` (climbs to a clickable ancestor when the target is not clickable, falls back to a tap gesture when nothing is, optionally verifies a condition after the click), `clickIfExists` / `clickAny` / `findAny`, `scrollUntil(target, options?)` (scrolls a container until the target shows, by accessibility actions or gestures, treating repeated unchanged content as the end), `typeInto(target, text, options?)` (a selector / an index / the focused field; replace or append; re-read verification and submit), `dismissPopups(targets, options?)` (closes one / every popup, or with `watch: true` returns a background guard handle driven by window change events), `collectList(container, item, options?)` (scrolls and collects items, deduplicated by content), `launchAndWait` / `backUntil` / `backToApp`, `toggle(target, checked)` (clicks only when the state differs, then verifies) and `retry(fn, options?)`; Flow gains the matching steps `.smartClick()` / `.scrollUntil()` / `.typeInto()` / `.dismissPopups()` / `.collectList()` / `.launchAndWait()` / `.backUntil()` / `.backToApp()` / `.toggle()` and the `flow.*` roots; every failure is a `FlowError` (`code` / `step` / `selector` / `reason`); `flow.defaults({ humanize: { offset, delay } })` gives the Flow action steps and the tools a human-like random tap offset and a pause before every action

Accessibility diagnostics: `auto.explain(selector, root?)` tallies a selector filter by filter (matches of each filter alone and what is left once the filters before it apply, the filter that leaves nothing, the near-miss nodes that pass every step before it), the result's `toString()` being the text report; `auto.dump(options?)` renders the window roots (or `root`) as a readable snapshot (indented text / JSON / uiautomator-style XML, with `maxDepth`, `properties`, `visibleOnly` and `maxNodes`); `UiObject.toJSON()` (so `JSON.stringify(node)` works) and `UiObject.dumpSubtree(options?)`; `auto.stats` holds the script's search / polled query / slowest selector / Flow step timings (`reset()` clears them, `toString()` is the text report); the layout inspector's code generator gains a "Code style" option that emits Flow-style snippets (such as `waitThenClick(selector).sync()`)

Event-driven waits: `waitForIdle(quietFor? | { quietFor?, timeout?, eventTypes? })` returns `{ quietFor, elapsed, events }` once no window state / content / windows-changed event has arrived for `quietFor` ms, replacing "sleep a while, then find"; `waitForEvent(type?, filter?, timeout?)` waits for the next accessibility event (the type a name, an array of names or `"*"`; the filter a function or `{ packageName, className, text }` with strings / regexes); `waitForToast(text?, timeout?)` and `waitForNotification(filter?, timeout?)` wait for another app's toast or a notification (substring / regex / function / object filters); all four exist as Flow roots (`flow.waitForIdle(...)` and so on) and chain steps (a chained `waitForIdle` passes the value through), and a timeout throws / rejects with a `FlowError` (`code` `TIMEOUT`); `auto.setFlags(["eventAssistedPolling"])` makes polling selector queries (`findOne(timeout)` / `untilFind()` and the like) and Flow waits retry as soon as an accessibility event arrives, the fallback interval of selector queries rising to 200 ms while nothing changes

Selector and node capabilities: the string selector syntax `select("text=Login clickable")` (whitespace-separated `key=value` / `key~=regex` or `key=/regex/flags` / `key` / `!key`, quotes around a value with spaces, an unquoted value with commas split into several arguments when needed as in `bounds=0,0,100,200`, the keys those of the selector registry; `UiSelector.select(String)` appends the filters and returns itself, so it chains with the builders; a malformed string throws with the character position, the offending term and candidate keys; `select()` without an argument stays the node action); `UiObject.isStale()` / `waitUntilGone(timeout?, interval?)` / `waitForStable(stableFor?, timeout?, interval?)` for node-level state checks and waits (default timeout 10 s, interval 50 ms; woken early by accessibility events under the `eventAssistedPolling` flag; refused on the UI thread); `findIterator()` for lazy finds (searched in `find()` order as the iteration advances, the rest of the tree left unwalked after a `break` in `for...of` or `close()`, `collect()` for the remaining nodes, `visited` / `produced` counters); window filter objects `{ type, packageName, title, displayId, active, focused, id, layer }` for `auto.setWindowFilter(...)` and the new `auto.findWindows(options?)` / `auto.findWindowRoots(options?)` (type names such as `application` / `inputMethod` / `system` / `accessibilityOverlay`, package name and title as a string or a regex, windows before API 30 counted on the default display)

Robustness (roadmap P5.5): a pending `waitForEvent` / `waitForIdle` / `waitForToast` / `waitForNotification` (synchronous or Flow form) ends at once with `A11Y_UNAVAILABLE` instead of timing out when the accessibility service is unbound meanwhile; Flow waits gain the `recoverService` option (also a default through `flow.defaults({ recoverService: true })`): a probe hitting a service outage then waits quietly for the service, one second at a time within the remaining timeout (an enabled but unbound service is re-enabled through the start strategies, the settings page is never opened and the user is asked at most once), the wait carries on with its target when the service returns in time and is otherwise rejected with an `A11Y_UNAVAILABLE` carrying `elapsed` / `attempts`; when the platform skips `onServiceConnected`, the registry adopts the instance from its first event and records the `adoptedByEvent` flag (`auto.state.adoptedByEvent`, a note on the in-process instance line of the service manager diagnostics), and the service info preferences (stable mode, gesture observing) are applied from that first event instead

Accessibility samples (roadmap P6.4): six scripts added to the in-app sample directory "无障碍服务" (Flow asynchronous waits and chained actions, toolkit form filling and popup dismissal, toolkit list scrolling and collection, string selectors and lazy iteration, selector diagnostics and node tree dumps, event-driven waits), each targeting the script's own floating window so that no other app is needed

The three title bar buttons of the floating console (minimize, layout state, close) are merged into a single "More" button whose menu offers Minimize, Resize, Input bar, Clear, Copy, Settings and Close; "Resize" enters a resize mode (the content dims and shows the current size, drag the right or bottom edge or the bottom-right corner to resize, tap elsewhere to leave); the "Settings" dialog toggles the time prefix, time format (presets or a custom pattern), log coloring, text size, status bar avoidance, and the title bar and content opacity

Console gains `setTimeVisible` / `setTimeFormat` / `setColorful` / `setAvoidStatusBar` / `setInputVisible` plus the matching `console.build` options (`timeVisible` / `timeFormat` / `colorful` / `avoidStatusBar` / `inputVisible`), mirroring the options of the floating window settings dialog; the more menus of the log page and the editor log panel add "Settings" (time prefix, time format, log coloring, text size) and an "Input bar" toggle, each remembered separately; new samples "Console/Time and coloring settings" and "Console/Order-independent settings"

Restores `console.rawInput(prompt?, ...args)` and `console.input(prompt?, ...args)` (abandoned since 6.3.1): they block the script thread until the user submits a line in the console input bar, and `input` evaluates the line as a JavaScript expression; the input bar is hidden by default and only appears while a script waits for input (the floating window shows itself and takes focus when nothing displays the console, and moves up to avoid the soft keyboard), or stays visible via `console.setInputVisible(true)` or the "Input bar" item of each console more menu; submitted text is echoed with a `> ` prefix and pending input is cancelled when the script ends; new sample "Console/Interactive input"

UI mode adds a `<globalconsole>` element showing the global console, while `<console>` now shows the console of the script itself (as in Auto.js 4); neither shows a time prefix by default; `<console global="true">` and the bare-attribute form `<console global>` are equivalent to `<globalconsole>` (layout XML now accepts bare attributes, treated as `"true"`); the element attributes cover the `console.setXxx` methods (`title` / `titleTextSize` / `titleTextColor` / `titleBackgroundColor` / `titleBackgroundTint` / `titleBackgroundAlpha` / `titleIconsTint` / `contentTextSize` / `contentTextColor` / `contentBackgroundColor` / `contentBackgroundTint` / `contentBackgroundAlpha` / `textSize` / `textColor` / `backgroundColor` / `backgroundTint` / `backgroundAlpha` / `timeVisible` / `timeFormat` / `colorful` / `inputVisible` and more), and setting `title` shows a title bar with a "More" menu; new sample "Layout/Console element"
Node.js bridge subscriptions push sensor, WebSocket, UI, overlay and input events through existing callbacks, with on/once/off listeners, bounded queues and compatible drainEvents
Optional idleExitMs releases an idle Node.js runtime process and reconnects for the next script, with idleForMs diagnostics and resident behavior preserved by default
Native stdin and readline accept console input, with execution-scoped JSON messages through autojs6:host and a backward-compatible v3 postMessage transaction
Node.js screen capture sessions use Android consent and the existing foreground service, with image handles, PNG/JPEG/WebP saving and cleanup when stopped or the script exits
Node.js image handles support clipping, resizing, grayscale, thresholding, template matching and color searches through the host image backend, with independent output handles and execution cleanup
Node.js image.toBytes transfers PNG or RGBA pixels through file descriptors into native Buffers, supports JNI and file bridge modes, and closes attachments after use, timeout or execution exit
Node device APIs expose live build, screen, battery and memory information, brightness control and timed screen wake locks; media supports setting stream volume, with Android permissions enforced

autojs6:events observes Android notifications, external Toast messages, accessibility keys and screen or battery broadcasts through push callbacks, with explicit permissions and automatic cleanup; native Node events remains unchanged

Node app supports Android service starts, broadcasts and installed package queries; dialogs supports text input, choices and progress windows with script cleanup, and keys provides accessibility system actions

Node recorder supports AAC recording with microphone permission, foreground disclosure, duration limits and script cleanup; ui.overlay supports declarative property updates, dragging and pushed events
Node scripts can run concurrently in two independent runtime processes, with a shared FIFO queue and execution-specific cancellation and input routing

MediaInfo queries support zero-based streamNumber, countGet stream counts, and infoKind for units, descriptions and readable names; Rhino and Node preserve default first-stream TEXT queries and negotiate extended plugin capabilities
Checks native ELF alignment before loading OpenCV and Image Quantization plugins, with a clear error for incompatible device page sizes
Plugin Center reads native page alignment from the official index and installed manifests, and warns before installing or enabling incompatible versions on 16 KB devices

MCP screenshot fallback: image.captureScreen(options) accepts the accessibility screenshot crop, scale, format and quality options and returns an encoded one-shot payload for descriptor transport; captureScreen() keeps returning an image handle, and missing or revoked MediaProjection consent returns a permission error.

`images.countPointsByColor(image, color, options?)` counts the pixels matching a color through an OpenCV mask, and `images.getMeanColor(image, region?)` returns the average color of an image or region
`images.readPixels` accepts an ImageWrapper in addition to a file path and leaves the passed image usable

`images.matchTemplate` and `images.findPointByImage` accept a `scales` option (one factor or a list) to match templates captured at other resolutions; every match now exposes `width`, `height`, `scale`, `center` and `rect`, and `MatchingResult` gains `size`, `isEmpty()`, `isNotEmpty()` and `filter()`
Floating run entry in the file explorer script menu, showing a translucent floating toolbar to start / stop the script, open it in the editor and view the log, following night mode and theme color

Layout inspector: long press an attribute in the node info dialog to select several and copy them as one chained selector (id('x').text('y')) or one object selector accepted by pickup() / detect(); "Save layout to file" writes the captured node tree to <working directory>/layouts/<time>.layout.json, and tapping such a file in the file explorer inspects it offline

3-Shell Terminal plugin integration: the drawer item and the project toolbar open the plugin's terminal, the directory menu "Open in terminal" is provided by the plugin (1.1.0 or later), the drawer switch follows the plugin's sessions, and a missing, disabled or incompatible plugin leads to the Plugin Center, the plugin settings or an update prompt
Script global object terminal: session management, visible execution and output events, with output waits and exit codes (requires the 3-Shell Terminal plugin) (see Sample Code > 终端)

`images.matchFeatures` accepts an image or path for either argument and detects features on the fly; new options `ransacThreshold`, `minInliers` and `maxFeatures`, `ObjectFrame` exposes `width`, `height`, `angle`, `bounds`, `points`, `matches` and `inliers`, and `ImageFeatures` exposes `count` and `method`

Accessibility companion contract for official plugins: companions that publish a `follow-host` service policy are enabled and disabled together with the AutoJs6 accessibility service using the configured root, secure settings or Shizuku strategies, and receive the host service state broadcast

Bun Runtime plugin project execution: a script below a directory carrying `project.json` or `package.json` is packed into a bounded workspace archive (at most 16384 entries and 64 MiB, regular files and directories only) for a plugin that declares `SUPPORTS_WORKSPACE_ARCHIVE`, so relative imports inside the project resolve; the entry file carries the current editor source, symbolic links and special files abort the run, and bare scripts or older plugins keep the single-source path

Bun Runtime plugin host info snapshot: when the plugin declares `SUPPORTS_HOST_INFO` and the `host_info` grant is on (default), `runScript` requests carry `hostInfoVersion = 1` and a `hostInfo` Bundle with the host package name, `BuildConfig.VERSION_DATE` and the preferred language tag, so Bun scripts can read the host/plugin/execution snapshot the plugin verifies and writes through the `AUTOJS6_HOST_INFO_FILE` environment variable; the host never sends its own version (the plugin resolves it through PackageManager), the grant is revocable per run (`BunHostCapabilityGrants`), and plugins without the capability receive exactly the previous request

Bun Runtime plugin capability bridge for dynamic calls with the first two capabilities `ui.toast` and `device.info`: when the plugin declares `SUPPORTS_HOST_CAPABILITY_BRIDGE` and at least one of the `ui_toast` / `device_info` grants is on (default), `runScript` requests carry `hostCapabilityBridgeVersion = 1`, a per-run `IBunHostCapabilityBroker` binder pinned to the plugin UID and execution ID, and the granted capability IDs; Bun scripts call `GET /v1/info` and `POST /v1/<capability>` over the plugin's unix socket, the host relays JSON uninterpreted (64 KiB requests, 256 KiB results, 1024 calls per run, 4 in flight, 10 s each) and answers through `IBunHostCapabilityCallback`. `ui.toast` shows at most four toasts per run from the main thread, `device.info` returns only `android.os.Build` facts; both switches live in the plugin's page of the Plugin Center, and plugins without the capability receive exactly the previous request

"Trash and version history" settings category: a retention policies sub-page edits version history (retention days, versions per file, size per file, total size, max tracked file size), trash (retention days, size limit) and emergency drafts (retention days, size limit), where 0 means unlimited and a change triggers a cleanup right away; plus an "Also clear version history when deleting permanently" switch
"Clean up now" and "Settings" entries in the trash and version history page menus, and a long press on either drawer item opens the retention policy settings
Client mode address dialog can scan the QR code shown by the VSCode extension (1.1.0+) to connect without typing the address
VSCode extension protocol v2 with request/response messages and remote file management methods (browse, read, write, rename and delete device files, run device scripts) for VSCode extension 1.1.0+

Version history list page: the editor and explorer entries now open a dedicated list showing time, size, operation and encoding per revision and marking the one identical to the current file; tap to preview, restore or delete, long-press for multi-selection delete, sort by time or size

Version history diff view: compare a revision with the current file, or select two revisions and compare them; added and removed lines are colored line by line, unchanged runs are folded and expandable, lines can be searched by text; oversized content shows line and size statistics only

Manual snapshots and pinning in version history: the editor menu gains "Create snapshot" (optional label) and snapshots are pinned by default; any revision can be pinned, unpinned or relabelled from the revision list, pinned revisions are exempt from the day / count / per-file size cleanup, and the global size cleanup removes unpinned revisions first

Version history export: the revision details dialog gains "Export", which writes the revision byte for byte (original encoding and BOM kept) to a chosen directory under a confirmed file name (the original name with the revision time stamp by default); overwriting a tracked file keeps its current content first

When version history is opened from the editor, the revision details dialog offers "Restore and save": after confirming the overwrite, the revision is loaded into the editor and saved to disk right away (the default "Restore" still only changes the editor content)

Trash multi-selection: long-press an item to start selecting, with select all / deselect all, batch restore (to each item's original path or one chosen directory; when names clash, choose skip / overwrite / auto-rename for the whole batch, and items sharing a name inside the batch are always auto-renamed; the progress dialog can be aborted and a summary reports restored / skipped / failed counts) and batch removal from the trash

Trash content preview: the item dialog gains "Preview", which opens text files in the read-only editor, lists the files inside a trashed directory (relative path, size, file and folder counts) and reports binary content instead of opening it

Trash item details: the item dialog gains "Details", showing name, type, original path, time moved to trash, size, SHA-256 and the expected expiry (with days and hours left) as selectable text that can be copied to the clipboard in one tap

After the explorer moves a file or directory to the trash, the snackbar offers "Undo", which restores each item to its original path only while that path is still free (never overwriting); items already gone from the trash or whose path is occupied are reported as skipped in the summary

The trash detects broken items whose data file is missing: the list marks them as "Data missing" in a highlight color, tapping offers only details and removal, and a new "Remove broken items" menu action clears them in one go; the periodic cleanup only logs their count and never deletes them automatically

VSCode extension connection: both client mode and server mode gain a "Manager" dialog (opened by the "Manager" button of the drawer entry or by long-pressing it) showing live status (connection state, server or listening address, peer host, extension and protocol versions, connection duration, last activity, reconnect session, last error; each row copyable), actions (connect, disconnect, reconnect now, stop reconnecting, start, stop, restart, disconnect all clients, copy address) and switches (auto reconnect, retry on network change, restore connection or start server on launch, notify on client changes); the server mode manager gains a "Clients" section listing every connected VSCode, with per-client details, disconnect and reconnect

VSCode extension connection: client mode reconnects automatically after an unexpected disconnect (extension crash, VSCode restart, network hiccup) with exponential backoff, immediate retry once a network is available and restore on app launch; both sides announce intentional closes with a bye message, so an explicit disconnect on either side is never followed by an automatic reconnect

VSCode extension connection: pairing confirmation - an unknown device connecting in client mode must be allowed in VSCode first (optionally remembered), while devices that scanned the QR code are trusted automatically; requires extension 1.1.0+
Server mode: LAN discovery (mDNS) - when enabled, the VSCode extension (1.1.0+) lists this device in its LAN connect picker, no address typing needed

VSCode remote files: chunked transfer - large files are read and written in 1 MiB pieces with progress shown in VSCode; requires extension 1.1.0+; fs.list can return file md5 on request so the extension can compare files when pulling project changes from the device
Client mode manager: a "History" entry in the control section shows the server addresses connected before; tap one to connect, long-press to delete, or clear them all

Mail plugin contract module (plugin-api/mail-api) with a frozen AIDL surface, a host client that opens account sessions on a dedicated binding lease, reopens them after the plugin process dies, retries once after an XOAUTH2 token refresh and streams attachments to disk through pipes, and Plugin Center registration as a default-on plugin

Script API `mail` of the mail plugin (mail roadmap P3.1 and P3.2): `mail.connect(options or alias)` with provider presets and a `tokenProvider` for XOAUTH2, `MailClient` with `test`, `send` (attachments from script paths through read-only descriptors), `folders` / `folder(path)` / `createFolder` / `deleteFolder` / `renameFolder`, `fetch`, `search` with a client-side fallback marker, `get` / `fetchBody`, `download` and `raw` streaming into the working directory with `onProgress`, `setFlags` with `markRead` / `markUnread` / `flag` / `unflag`, `move`, `copy`, `delete`, `expunge`, `append` and `close`, each with an `Async` Promise form settled on the script thread; message results carry `Date` fields, printable addresses and bound `load` / `download` methods, failures are `MailError` objects with `code` and `retryable`, and `mail.providers`, `mail.accounts`, `mail.setDefault` plus forwarders of every client method live on the global

Script API `mail.watch` of the mail plugin (mail roadmap P5): `client.watch(folder?, {mode?, pollIntervalMs?, fetchBody?, reconnect?})` and `mail.watch` return a `MailWatch` emitter whose `message(message, watch)`, `mode`, `resync`, `error` and single `close(reason)` events arrive on the script thread and keep the script alive until `stop()`; the plugin watches with IMAP IDLE (polling fallback, POP3 by UIDL), the host drops stale generations and out-of-order deliveries, a plugin death is reported as `PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE` and by default followed by a new watch on the reopened session with a `resync`, and closing the client or leaving the script stops its watches

Mail plugin contract version 2 with background watches (mail roadmap P8): the appended `IMailPlugin.openTrigger` / `listTriggers` and the `IMailTrigger` / `IMailTriggerCallback` interfaces subscribe to the watches the plugin keeps running in its own foreground service, and the new "On mail arrived" intent task (`org.autojs.autojs6.action.MAIL_TRIGGER`, received behind the host's signature permission) launches a script for each new message of a chosen watch, optionally filtered by sender and subject, with the event document in `engines.myEngine().execArgv.mail`; repeated deliveries are dropped and bursts are throttled to one launch per task every 3 s; a version 1 plugin never sees the new calls

EPUB plugin contract module (plugin-api/epub-api) with a frozen AIDL surface for book extraction (metadata, table of contents, reading order, chapter text, resources, search) and token-based reader sessions, the host discovery wrapper of the `epub` engine, and Plugin Center registration of the Readium EPUB Reader package, whose Explorer Action and EPUB services share one entry

EPUB plugin host client (core/plugin/epub, plugin roadmap P5.4): `EpubPluginHost.openBook` validates the path, opens it read-only and hands out a book client (metadata, table of contents, reading order, paged chapter text as plain text or Markdown, resource export through a spooled pipe, search, positions) on a dedicated binding lease with a death recipient; `openReader` opens a reader session, reads its one-time token and starts the plugin's reader Activity itself (two-step launch), bridges the session events (open, progress, bookmark, error, close) with generation and sequence checks, and forwards goTo, navigate, setPreferences, getBookmarks and getState; every failure maps to the contract's error codes

Script API `epub` of the Readium EPUB Reader plugin (plugin roadmap P6.1): `epub.open(path or options)` returns an `EpubBook` with `metadata`, `toc` (a `{ title, href, children }` tree), `readingOrder`, `positions`, `text(target?, options?)` (an href, a reading-order index, a table-of-contents entry or the whole book, paged with `offset` / `maxChars` and `format` text or markdown), `textAll`, `cover` (an `Image` or a file), `resource`, `search` and `close`; the convenience layer `epub.metadata` / `toc` / `readingOrder` / `text` / `cover` / `search` opens and closes the book per call, `epub.isAvailable()` probes the plugin, each method has an `Async` Promise form settled on the script thread, paths follow the script's working directory and refuse URIs, failures are `EpubError` objects with `code`, the plugin-unavailable hint is localized, and the script's exit closes the books it left open

Reader control of the `epub` script API (plugin roadmap P6.2): `epub.read(path, options?)` opens the reader of the Readium EPUB Reader plugin and returns an `EpubReaderSession` event emitter whose `open`, `progress`, `bookmark`, `error` and `close` events arrive on the script thread, with `goTo(href | progression | locator)`, `next` / `prev` / `nextChapter` / `prevChapter`, `setPreferences(partial)`, `bookmarks()`, `close({ finish? })` and the properties `locator`, `progress`, `title`, `chapterTitle`, `href`, `positions`, `state`, `reason`, `isOpen` / `isClosed`; the start position comes from `href`, `progression` or `locator` with optional `preferences`, a script that stops draining its events gets `error(LIMIT_EXCEEDED)` and `close(overflow)`, and the script's exit ends the session while the reader stays open for the user

EPUB samples (plugin roadmap P6.3): three scripts added to the new in-app sample directory "电子书" (EPUB 元数据与目录: metadata, table of contents, reading order and positions of a book found under Download or Books; 导出章节文本: chapter and whole-book text export as plain text or Markdown, cover export and full-text search; 打开阅读器并监听进度: a reader session with `open` / `progress` / `bookmark` / `error` / `close` listeners, start preferences, a chapter turn and `close()` that leaves the reader to the user); every script checks `epub.isAvailable()` first and explains how to install the Readium EPUB Reader plugin

EPUB contract version 2 with highlights and notes (plugin roadmap P9.4): the appended `IEpubBook.getAnnotations` (paged, in reading order) and the `highlight` reader-session event carry the reader's highlights and notes as an `annotations` document (id, style, color, note, quote, chapter title, locator, createdAt, updatedAt); the host negotiates the version from the plugin's `epubMaxContractVersion` and stamps it on every request, so version-1 plugins never see the new call; the `epub` script API gains `book.annotations()` and `epub.annotations(path)` with their `Async` forms, and `EpubReaderSession` emits `highlight({ action, id, style, color, note, quote, title, locator, createdAt, updatedAt })` with `action` added, updated or removed

Calling the compat accessors `getChild()` / `getParent()` etc. on a `UiObject` that carried a node allocator recursed endlessly (the allocator called back into the wrapper's own accessors); the allocator now works on the raw node and registers by object identity rather than node equality (two instances of the same view are no longer released as one). It is still not wired into script runtimes: below Android 13 nodes are pooled per process, so a batch release at exit could recycle an instance already reused by another script
The selector condition `contextClickable()` showed up as `checkable` in the selector's string form (`selector().toString()`, error messages)
The global function form `filter(fn)` failed with "Invalid arguments", and a regex inside a map selector array (`pickup({text: [/regex/]})`) was rejected

Decimals in the string form of selectors (`selector().toString()`, error messages) showed up as `boundsLeft(0,5)` under UI languages whose decimal separator is a comma (French, Russian, ...); a dot is used everywhere now

Java exceptions thrown by the global function form of selector methods (`algorithm('xyz')`, `textMatch('(')`, ...) could not be caught by the script's `try / catch` and terminated the script; they are thrown as catchable script errors now

With the `findOnUiThread` flag set, a search posted to the UI thread could hang forever when its wake-up was lost (the UI thread finished the search before the script thread started waiting), and `findOne(timeout)` never timed out while the UI thread was blocked; the wait is now bounded by the query's timeout and cannot miss the wake-up

`UiObject.clickBounds()` prepared a Looper on the script thread and called `quit()` once the gesture finished, which quit the script thread's own event loop: `setTimeout` and other callbacks never ran afterwards and the script ended early; nodes obtained from a query now tap through the script's gesture dispatcher (the servant Looper), and nodes from other sources (such as the `source` of an `auto.registerEvent` callback) wait for the result on a shared callback thread without touching the calling thread's Looper; on the main thread (for example in a `"ui"` script) the call failed because the main Looper may not quit

The `pickup` / `detect` result type `['compass', 'p']` always failed with "unknown result type" because `compass` was listed with a `String` parameter in the interceptor table while its signature takes `CharSequence`; it works now

When the layout inspector generated code for a child of a collection widget without an action selected, the generated `forEach` block contained the invalid statement `target.;`; the line is omitted now
Text and controls in layout inspector floating windows and dialogs had insufficient contrast with some theme colors or in night mode
Incomplete escaping of quotes, backslashes, and control characters in Layout Inspector "Copy as selector" and selector string output

Layout Inspector code generation ignored text-setting and some query actions, expanded a single list target into actions on the whole group, used deprecated query calls, silently fell back from Flow or failed on long presses, and located same-named IDs across packages incorrectly

Of several overloads with the same name on a widget collection array only the last one survived (such as `performAction(action)` next to `performAction(action, ...args)`), so calling it with the other number of arguments failed with a parameter mismatch; all overloads are bound per name now

Since 6.7.0 Alpha13 a plain string passed to the `contains` selector family (`textContains` / `descContains` / `contentContains` / `idContains` / `classNameContains` / `packageNameContains` etc.) was compiled as a regex pattern (`textContains(".")` matched any non-empty text, `textContains("1+1")` matched "11", `textContains("(")` threw); it is a literal substring again, consistent with `text(s)` / `textStartsWith` / `textEndsWith`; pass a regex (`textContains(/re/i)`) or use `textMatch` / `textMatches` for patterns, and a string in the form "/re/flags" is no longer treated as a regex by `contains`

`requestFocus()` / `disableFocus()` of floating windows (`floaty.rawWindow` / `floaty.window`) updated the layout of the attached window right on the script thread and occasionally threw `CalledFromWrongThreadException`; they now run on the UI thread (like `setSize` / `setPosition`)

The accessibility notification observer (behind `events.observeToast()` and the like) treated every system notification as another app's toast (its notification check named this app's own subclass, which never matches), so notifications never reached its notification listeners and other apps' notifications were misreported as toasts; it now checks the framework's `android.app.Notification`

The call order of `console.setPosition` / `setSize` / `setGravity` and `console.show()` affected the result (e.g. `console.show(); console.setPosition(500, 400)` needed a `sleep` in between, and the reverse order could drop the setting); settings are now recorded and applied once the window is attached, so order and timing no longer matter

Dragging the floating console by its title bar occasionally failed (the drag gesture was bound before the window was attached and raced with button clicks and window closing); the title bar drag is now set up after attachment, the movement is clamped to the screen and the position is recorded when the drag ends

The floating console had a 12dp margin on every side, so `console.setPosition(0, 0)` could not reach the screen edge; the margin is removed, the Y coordinate starts below the status bar by default (disable with `setAvoidStatusBar(false)`), and both the position and the size are clamped to the screen

The MCP Server session controller could publish the `starting` snapshot pulled right after `openServer` on top of a `running` status the plugin had already delivered through its callback, so `status` never reported the listener as running; the pulled snapshot is now published only when no callback status arrived while it was in flight

The side drawer kept showing outdated MCP Server guidance such as "not installed" after the plugin was installed, enabled or updated, until AutoJs6 was restarted; an installed plugin that Android has not activated yet now shows "Activation required" before the switch is used
MediaInfo details and snapshots show the original source path in Complete name instead of a private cache or descriptor path, while preserving the snapshot display filename

Node bridge `accessibility.swipe` / `accessibility.gesture` (the coordinate gestures of the MCP Server and Node plugins) answered `false` (cancelled) for every gesture after the first one on a reused broker dispatch thread: the gesture automator without a handler prepared a Looper on the calling thread and quit it once the first gesture completed, so the next call on that thread returned at once and its real result went to a dead handler; the bridge now hands the automator the main-looper handler, as the Python host broker does

OpenCV and ImageQuant plugin policies rejected native libraries built with NDK r28c (28.2.13676358) as a native NDK version mismatch, which blocked the rebuilt OpenCV plugin v1.1.2; both r26b and r28c builds are now accepted
The OpenCV and Image Quantization plugin loaders continued after read-only cache protection failed; native files are now verified as read-only before loading for Android 17 compatibility
runtime.loadDex on Android 7.0 / 7.1 could overwrite the staged DEX with ART's optimized output, causing class loading to fail
Dynamically loaded Kotlin compilers failing due to restricted Unsafe atomics or a missing reflection runtime
Legacy Rhino scope reflection APIs preventing external libraries from automatically registering Java/Kotlin classes
MediaProjection bridge captures retry transient missing frames up to six times, allowing consecutive screenshots after the capture pipeline refreshes without requesting consent again

OpenCV matrices behind `images.imread`, `images.matToImage` and Mat-backed images were either never released or shared a native header with a source that could be garbage collected, causing native memory leaks and dangling pointers
A finishing script recycled the images of every other running script; images are now registered and recycled per script runtime
`colors.isSimilar` and `images.detectColor` with the `hs` algorithm matched any color, and `colors.rgb` / `colors.rgba` treated fractional or percentage components as integers
`images.isEqual` returned true for images differing in a single channel, `images.mse` saturated at `255`, and `images.ncc` / `images.isGrayscale` mishandled grayscale or RGBA input

`images.invert` dropped the alpha channel, `ImageWrapper.saveTo` wrote Mat-backed images with swapped red and blue channels, and `images.clip` silently produced wrong results for regions outside the image

Images passed by path to `images.clip`, `images.findCircles` and `images.readPixels` could be recycled before use, and `images.findImage` / `images.matchTemplate` could throw or return wrong matches for templates near the image border or larger than the search region
`images.load` applies a 30-second timeout and closes its connection, and `images.saveBitmap`, feature matching and histogram comparison release their temporary streams and matrices

Template matching returned coordinates rounded to a coarse pyramid level (off by up to several pixels) once a match reached the threshold early, could report the same location twice for neighbouring candidates, and returned results unsorted and beyond `max`

`images.matchTemplate` threw for an image and template with different channel counts, never matched a solid-color template, and `useTransparentMask` masked only the alpha channel instead of the transparent pixels; `MatchingResult.sortBy(compareFn)` failed when the comparator returned a non-integer number

`images.matchFeatures` returned a wrongly sized frame when the object features were computed with a `scale` other than 1, re-sorted the corners so a rotated object lost the correspondence to its own corners, could return a distorted frame from an unreliable homography, drew the `drawMatches` image from the descriptor matrices instead of the images, and threw an OpenCV error for images without key points
`images.detectAndComputeFeatures` leaked its intermediate matrices, and ORB found no key points at all in images smaller than 63 px and only a few in small objects because of the default 31 px border

The MCP Server session controller rebound the plugin about one second after the user force-stopped it in the system settings, which started it again against that decision; a plugin that is no longer available after its process died (stopped, disabled or uninstalled) is not rebound any more, the drawer switch closes and its subtitle shows the activation guide the way a fresh install does

Version history now fingerprints the content after a save, so the next save of a renamed or moved file re-attaches to its existing history; re-attaching by fingerprint only happens when the old path is gone, so an identical copy no longer takes over the original file's history
Trash and version history resolve the internal storage root from the current user's actual path instead of a fixed /storage/emulated/0, so they work in multi-user and work profile environments

Restoring a version to disk, or restoring a file from the trash with overwrite, first records the target's current content as a RESTORE_PRE revision; trash overwrite restores write to a temporary file and replace the target afterwards, so an abort or crash no longer leaves a half-written file
Auto rename on a trash restore conflict decides directories by the item type, so a directory with a dot in its name (such as my.project) no longer has an extension split off
The version history dialog lists every retained revision (previously at most 20), offers Preview from the editor entry as well, and keeps its mode after a revision is deleted and the list reloads
Orphan blob cleanup for version history now protects blobs younger than 30 minutes, so a fresh snapshot whose database row is still pending is no longer deleted

DEX compiler diagnostics now preserve bounded redacted INFO/WARNING/ERROR details with optional logical origin, archive entry, and position metadata; Developer options show the process-local last JAR route and localized BUSY, timeout, and fallback guidance

Improved formatting performance for large arrays in the Rhino console

Added phase-by-phase Node.js startup timing and trustworthy cold/runtime-warm performance reporting
Cached built-in Node.js native library resolution to avoid repeated plugin discovery
Cached authorized external Node.js runtime candidates and persistent Binder sessions with state invalidation and atomic reconnection to reduce discovery and bind overhead
Removed project-wide encrypted-module scans from the default Node.js execution path to improve startup performance for non-trivial scripts and large projects
Added real multi-round Rhino/Node engine-switch regression coverage for script execution, persistent external-plugin session reuse and recovery, and clean teardown
Added persistent external-plugin runtime soak testing and Node.js production-evidence gates covering device/ABI matrices, runtime lifecycle, resource metrics, and 8-hour/24-hour stability

HTML and Markdown previews are delegated to dedicated Previewer plugins; the main app keeps the entry and guides installation or enabling when the plugin is missing, disabled, or unavailable
Consolidated all Pinyin calls through the corresponding plugin and removed the unused built-in dictionary and conversion implementation

Starting or stopping the accessibility service through root or secure settings no longer writes the system's `accessibility_enabled` value (maintained by the system itself from the bound services since Android 7.0), so stopping this service no longer leaves a stale 0 behind while other accessibility services stay enabled
Floating windows such as the floating button with its dialogs and the layout inspector now follow AutoJs6's own language and night mode settings instead of the system's

The floating button "More" menu opens without waiting for foreground app queries, loads information in the background and refreshes only the affected subtitles; package and Activity share one query, and dismissing the menu cancels pending loads and discards late results

The `source` of the event object received by `auto.registerEvent` callbacks is now resolved on first access (every event used to walk the parent chain eagerly for its depth and index), which lowers the cost of callbacks that never read it; below API 33 a `source` that was not read during the callback is null afterwards

Accessibility window root resolution now has a single implementation (`AccessibilityBridge` rewritten in Kotlin, its three duplicated code paths unified in `WindowRootPolicy` / `WindowRootProvider`, which the layout inspector uses for its windows as well): with a window filter set, `auto.root` moves on to the next window when the first passing window has no root (it used to return `null` right away); `auto.windowRoots` and node actions can no longer meet a `null` root; the fact that `auto.rootInActiveWindow` ignores the window filter is now stated explicitly in the sources

Accessibility node recycling is now decided in one place, `NodeLifecycle` / `NodeRecyclePolicy` (nodes need no recycling from Android 13 on, so the no-op `recycle()` is no longer called for each of them; the inline recycling formerly scattered over the search algorithms, scroll actions, the service's cached root and the allocator all goes through it, and a failing recycle is logged instead of aborting a search)

Accessibility screenshots (`automator.captureScreen()`) are taken by the new `A11yScreenshotter`: the hardware buffer behind a screenshot is now always closed (only the wrapping bitmap used to be recycled), and the retry on the system's rate-limit error is capped at 60 attempts (3 s), after which the promise resolves to `null` like for any other failure (it used to never resolve while the system kept rate limiting)

Selector filters, the search algorithms (DFS / BFS) and the compass walk (`compass`) now work against the Android-free `UiNode` interface (implemented by `UiObject`), so all three are covered by JVM unit tests over an in-memory node tree; the script-facing API and behaviour are unchanged

Selector properties are now described once in the declarative `SelectorRegistry`: the `UiSelector` builder methods are generated from it, map selectors (`pickup({...})` etc.) are parsed by it instead of by reflection, and the global selector functions are exported from it plus an explicit whitelist (`toStringReadable` and the mangled names of `internal` members are no longer exposed as globals); numeric arguments of global functions and map selectors are uniformly rounded to integers (map selectors used to truncate)

Selector filters deduplicated: the string properties (text / desc / content / id / className / packageName and their variants) share `StringPropertyFilter`, the bounds metrics (left / boundsLeft / minLeft / maxLeft etc.) share `MetricsFilter`, the integer properties share `IntFilter`; the screen-relative filters (bounds / metrics / screenCenter / screenCoverage) evaluate against an injectable screen size and are covered by JVM unit tests; a selector evaluates a snapshot of its filter list, so one selector shared between threads is safe; the script-facing API and behaviour are unchanged

Selector queries (`findOne(timeout)` / `untilFind` / `untilFindOne` / `exists` / `find(max)` and the deprecated `findOne()` / `waitFor()`) run as a polling plan (`PollPolicy`: timeout, interval, times, backoff) with unchanged defaults (50 ms interval, a timeout of 0 or less waits forever); the methods that wait without limit are marked "may block forever" in their KDoc; with the `findOnUiThread` flag set, a search posted to the UI thread waits at most the query's timeout and fails with a readable error once it passes (`findOne(timeout)`), while unbounded queries (`untilFind` etc.) wait interruptibly so that stopping the script ends them

`UiObject` split up: the alias table of the `pickup` / `detect` result types, the picker and the interceptor that calls node methods by name moved to `core/automator/pick` (`PickResultType` / `Picker` / `Detector` / `Invoker`), `summary()` / `toString()` / `isSimilar()` to `UiObjectSummary`; new `UiObject.fingerprint()` (a hash of bounds, text, description, class name, child count and the key boolean properties, without visiting siblings or children); `indexInParent()` of a node reached through `parent()` is computed on first use; the layout inspector's code generator (`CodeGenerator` / `ReadOnlyUiObject`) converted to Kotlin, the latter now a snapshot view implementing `UiNode` directly; the script-facing API and behaviour are unchanged

Cross-runtime reuse (roadmap P5.4): the Python host's selector capabilities (`selector.snapshot` / `selector.find` / `selector.click` / `selector.set_text`) and the Node Bridge's `accessibility` module (`findOne` / `findAll` / `click` / `longClick` / `setText` / `scrollForward` / `scrollBackward` / `findByText` / `clickText`) now consume the script runtime's accessibility core (the `UiNode` walk, the selector filters, the window root provider, the node lifecycle), both JSON wire protocols staying identical field by field; Node Bridge searches no longer leak the nodes visited on the way below Android 13; the Python host's accessibility screenshots take their single attempts through the shared `A11yScreenshotter` (keeping the host's bounded retry and 4-second deadline)

Every script runtime now owns its console (its own log entries and floating window, with every line forwarded to the global console); the floating window only shows the output of the current script (as in Auto.js 4) and re-running a script with the same title replaces the floating window left by the previous run; log entries store the raw content and a timestamp and each view renders the time prefix on demand (hidden by default in the floating window, switchable in the log page settings); Node bridge `console.tail` entries gain a `time` field (epoch milliseconds) while `text` keeps its time prefix
Screen OCR examples request Android capture consent and recognize real image handles; unavailable OCR or barcode plugins return readable unavailable errors, while recognition failures remain errors

Node scripts support negotiated asynchronous startup, releasing Binder threads during long-running execution and returning workspace changes after terminal completion, with legacy synchronous host compatibility

Node bridge `accessibility.dump` JSON nodes carry the state flags `scrollable`, `checkable`, `checked`, `editable`, `focused`, `selected` and `longClickable` next to the seven descriptor fields; the MCP Server session grant includes the `keys.notifications` / `quickSettings` / `powerDialog` / `lockScreen` global actions for the plugin's `ui_press_key` tool, and a `keys.*` call without the accessibility service now answers the `unavailable` category like the `accessibility` module; a zero-length `accessibility.swipe` (identical end points) is dispatched as a press of `durationMs`, which the coordinate forms of the MCP `ui_click` / `ui_long_click` tools rely on
Host and runtime-kit native libraries support 16 KB alignment, with rebuilt jackpal JNI libraries, NDK r28.2 libc++, provenance records and shared build verification
APK Builder reports incompatible native libraries in build progress and results, and records alignment in local build-input metadata while preserving compressed packaging
Plugin Center version summaries also normalize ISO 8601 date-time strings such as `2026-09-11T14:30:00+08:00` to `yyyy-MM-dd`, keeping the calendar date of the string's own offset
Multi-color matching (`images.findPointByColors`, `images.findPointsByColors`) pre-filters candidates with vectorized OpenCV masks, running tens of times faster on dense images with identical results

Color detectors expose a `distance` method shared by `colors.isSimilar`, `images.detectColor` and multi-color matching; the `hs` algorithm uses circular hue distance and unknown algorithm names raise a descriptive error
Screen capturer state is read without locking, and `images.releaseScreenCapturer` no longer blocks concurrent image calls while releasing

Pyramid levels of template matching use area interpolation, masked matching keeps the normalized correlation coefficient, and small `max` values still refine several candidates so the best match is not lost at coarse levels

Layout hierarchy window: rows summarize id / text / desc / clickable and other flags, the selected node and all of its ancestors are highlighted in the tree and outlined on screen, the tree scrolls sideways, a "Select parent node" menu item walks the selection upwards, and a one-time tip explains exiting with the volume down key

Feature matching keeps only RANSAC inliers and validates the projected quadrilateral, corrects a matcher incompatible with the descriptor type instead of throwing, accepts `scale` above 1 to enlarge small objects, and ORB detects up to 20000 key points by default so textured scenes no longer starve the object region

Node bridge adds the read-only app.listDocs / app.readDoc (enumerate and read the verified offline documentation assets of the installed AutoJs6-Plugin-Offline-Docs, paths confined to the docs root, 1 MiB per read, available: false without an eligible plugin) so that the MCP Server plugin can expose autojs6://docs/ resources
Retention limits for version history and trash (days, versions, per-file bytes, total bytes, tracked file size) treat zero or negative values uniformly as unlimited and share one policy object
Version history skips a snapshot whose content is identical to the newest stored revision, avoiding duplicate storage

Moving items to the trash checks the size limit first and, when the items exceed it, offers to move anyway, delete permanently or cancel; older entries are evicted right after the move, and the size limit always keeps the newest entry

The periodic cleanup applies the complete retention policy (days, versions, per-file and total size for version history; days and size for the trash) and drops file entries that own no revisions; emergency draft limits treat 0 as unlimited as well

VSCode extension connections gain an application-level heartbeat (ping/pong) and a frame length limit, releasing dead connections promptly and avoiding huge allocations on desync _[`issue #333`](http://issues.autojs6.com/333)_ _[`issue #523`](http://issues.autojs6.com/523)_
Files saved from the VSCode extension can keep their relative directory structure inside the working directory _[`vscode-ext issue #37`](http://vscext-project.autojs6.com/issues/37)_
The explorer records the current content of a file as an OVERWRITE_PRE revision before a copy or move replaces it; when a directory is overwritten, the tracked files inside get snapshots
Each trash list item shows an expiry countdown (derived from the trash retention days, hidden when unlimited), and items expiring within 24 hours are highlighted
When a trash item cannot be previewed or restored because its data file is missing or damaged, a localized message is shown instead of the raw exception text

When a trash item is restored to a location other than its original path, the version history of the file (or of every file under the directory) follows it to the new path; moving a file to the trash records the version history entry it was linked to at that time

A damaged directory archive in the trash no longer aborts the whole restore: readable entries are restored as usual, damaged ones are recorded and skipped (half-written files are removed), the restored / failed counts are reported at the end, and the item stays in the trash

The version history file list shows the same file-type icons as the explorer; the version history and trash lists now refresh incrementally by diff, so stat / countdown / selection changes no longer redraw the whole list

installer installation options accept grantAllRequestedPermissions, requestUpdateOwnership, dexopt, installReason and packageSource when supported by the selected plugin; omission preserves existing behavior, while explicit false/none still requires support
